stories.headline: Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff
stories.summary: President Trump said Friday that deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller will take over Monday after midterm losses, while Wiles shifts to political operations; Miller has been a central architect of Trump's immigration agenda.

stories.headline: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
stories.summary: Tech bounced Friday from its worst drubbing in over a year, with the semiconductor index up 4.2%, but the Nasdaq still fell 3.4% for the week; October payrolls beat expectations, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and traders lifted bets on a December Fed rate hike.

stories.headline: Union Pacific derails about 20 coal cars in Polk County, Iowa
stories.summary: A Union Pacific train derailed about 5 a.m. Wednesday near Highway 65 between Des Moines and Carlisle; about 20 coal cars left the tracks with no injuries, no hazardous-materials concerns, and no road closures, officials said.

stories.headline: Republican Jake Bockenfeld wins Douglas County commissioner seat
stories.summary: Bockenfeld leads Democrat Irene Bonham about 51% to 49% in District 1, the closest Douglas County commissioner race in at least a decade, with roughly 800 ballots still outstanding as of Thursday.

breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 501 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Nov. 6 close (mimics MMFI). Breadth slipped slightly even as the indexes bounced, since Friday's gains were concentrated in chip stocks.

fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed edged up to 22 from 20 after Friday's close but stays in extreme fear, well below 26 a week ago and 47 a month ago as investors digest this week's AI-led sell-off.

markets.summary: Stocks steadied Friday after Thursday's AI-led rout but still logged a rough week: the S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86 (down 2.7% on the week), the Nasdaq gained 1.09% to 24,579.43 (down 3.4%, its fourth straight weekly loss and still in correction), and the Dow slipped 0.46% to 51,285.73. Tech led the bounce as chip stocks recovered part of their losses, though the Nasdaq sits below its 40-week average with RSI near 34 and MACD under its signal line. Small caps edged up, with the Russell 2000 gaining 0.89% to 2,754 but still below its 40-week average. Rates stayed firm after a stronger-than-expected October jobs report, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.86% and traders raising odds of a December Fed hike, per Reuters. Gold futures dipped 0.94% to about $4,075 and silver 0.82% to about $51.80, though both gained more than 4% on the week and remain below their 40-week averages.

stories.headline: Why SpaceX stock jumped 8% Friday
stories.summary: SpaceX rose 8.6% to $134.27 after Elon Musk predicted government contracts would fall below 10% of fourth-quarter revenue and said revenue could grow about 70% from the prior quarter.

stories.headline: FAA plan to streamline launch licensing helps SpaceX rebound
stories.summary: Investing.com tied part of the bounce to an FAA proposal to streamline commercial launch and re-entry rules, plus ARK Invest buying about $47.4 million of shares earlier in the week.

stories.headline: SpaceX Texas land deal and Tesla merger dealt election blow
stories.summary: IBD says a Texas land purchase could be delayed until Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office, and some analysts think a Democratic Congress dims chances of a Tesla-SpaceX merger.

stories.headline: Nvidia and other AI chip stocks rebound after sell-off
stories.summary: Nvidia rose 2.8% to $186.64 Friday after crashing 9.3% Thursday in the tech rout.

stories.headline: House chairmen ask Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing
stories.summary: Three House committee chairmen asked Nvidia's CEO to address his interactions with a Megaspeed executive and the company's safeguards against foreign espionage, proposing a Nov. 18 briefing; the request makes no accusation of wrongdoing.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
headlines.summary: Tech bounced Friday from its worst drubbing in over a year, with the semiconductor index up 4.2%, but the Nasdaq still fell 3.4% for the week; October payrolls beat expectations, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and traders lifted bets on a December Fed rate hike.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq and S&P 500 rebound, Dow slips to cap bruising week for AI stocks
headlines.summary: The S&P 500 still posted its worst week since June as investors weighed what Democrats' midterm sweep means for data-center construction and AI spending.

stories.headline: County Line Road intersection closures begin Nov. 9 in Highlands Ranch
stories.summary: Douglas County will close E. Phillips Avenue at County Line Road for about a week starting as early as Nov. 9 for storm-sewer work, then close Clarkson Street at County Line for about a week starting Nov. 16, as part of the $30 million widening project.

stories.headline: Federal judge pauses Trump's planned 250-foot triumphal arch
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a 14-day hold on construction of the proposed Military Triumphal Arch near Arlington National Cemetery hours after the National Capital Planning Commission voted 8-4 to approve the project.

stories.headline: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested over bank collapse
stories.summary: Senators unanimously removed Peña after the Ueno Bank failure left an estimated three million depositors without access to savings; Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president through 2028.

stories.summary: President Trump said Friday that deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller will take over Monday after midterm losses, while Wiles shifts to political operations; Miller has been a central architect of Trump's immigration agenda.

stories.headline: Newsom moves to commute all 548 California death sentences
stories.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom told the California Supreme Court he will commute every death sentence to life without parole; about 40% he can commute directly, while the rest need high-court approval in a state that has not executed anyone since 2006.

stories.headline: MSU men's soccer falls 3-2 at No. 4 Indiana, draws No. 4 seed in Big Ten Tournament
stories.summary: A second-half comeback with goals from Andrew Darakdjian and Richie Ludwig left Michigan State short in the regular-season finale; the Spartans (10-4-3, 5-3-2 Big Ten) face No. 5 Maryland on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Bloomington.

stories.headline: No. 5 MSU women's soccer meets Michigan in Big Ten Tournament semifinals Sunday
stories.summary: After Bella Najera's overtime winner knocked out Washington, the Spartans draw in-state rival Michigan at 2 p.m. ET Sunday on Big Ten Network in St. Louis; Michigan upset top seed Ohio State 2-1 in the quarters.

stories.headline: MSU punter Rhys Dakin named to Ray Guy Award midseason watch list
stories.summary: The junior transfer from Iowa leads the Big Ten at 49.3 yards per punt and faces Michigan on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET in Ann Arbor on Peacock with the Paul Bunyan Trophy on the line.

stories.headline: California No Longer Prosecuting Murderers Who Kill Fewer Than 950 People
stories.summary: In a Babylon Bee satire tied to Newsom's death-row commutations, the governor supposedly aligns California's murder threshold with retail theft limits so killers of fewer than 950 people can walk.

stories.headline: Dante Confirms First Circle Of Hell Is Iowa
stories.summary: Literary scholars in this Babylon Bee piece re-read Inferno and decide Limbo was Iowa all along, a finding Iowa residents say they always kind of suspected.

stories.headline: Uncarved Pumpkin Struggling With Survivor's Guilt
stories.summary: The Onion reports a Raleigh pumpkin still intact nearly a week after Halloween is racked with shame that it alone escaped carving and porch duty.

weather.summary: A Northeast low brings heavy rain and a Slight Risk of excessive rainfall over parts of New England into Sunday morning, while SPC has a Slight Risk of severe storms over eastern North Carolina through Saturday morning. Great Lakes rain ends over Michigan by Saturday afternoon, Southwest and Southern Plains storms continue through Sunday, and a new Pacific system brings Northwest coastal rain Saturday evening into Sunday morning before high pressure returns.
